problems.problem: The run-review export fix cannot work as written. Changing only find_backchain_loops finds directories that every reader still parses in the old layout. Also, nothing defines where a ShipLoop host puts a 0.7.0 Backchain run directory.
problems.evidence: export.py loop_doc reads `receipt_path = loop / "until-loop-receipt.json"` (L1043). _passes reads only review-records/action-N-review.json or review-NN.json (L871-886). The collector falls back to `loop / "until-loop-receipt.json"` (L3238). find_graph_check_dirs (L1159-1164) classes any backchain/<action>/ directory that has check-*.json and no until-loop-receipt.json as graph-check-only, so a 0.7.0 run directory would also be listed a second time as 'no loop'. A 0.7.0 run keeps loop/receipt.json, cycles/NN/{review,report}.json and evidence.json (backchain.py Run, L404-414). prepare refuses a non-empty directory (L556). The `backchain-check` verb writes check-*.json into RUN/backchain/<action>/ (backchain-route.md, graph check paragraph), so the host cannot reliably prepare in that directory. Backchain SKILL.md L52 says 'Use a new, empty run directory: where the caller or request lets you write, otherwise outside the project'. No ShipLoop packet, guide or reference names a location (grep of skills/shiploop for 'prepare --run', 'loop/receipt.json' and 'run directory' finds nothing).
problems.fix: Replace the W1 export bullet with this text: '(a) The plan packet names the Backchain run directory: `prepare --run RUN/backchain/<action>/run`, a fresh empty subdirectory. (b) export.py finds `backchain/*/run/loop/receipt.json`. loop_doc reads that receipt and the cycles from `evidence.json` and `cycles/NN/review.json`, and the collector's start-time fallback (L3238) uses it. find_graph_check_dirs leaves out a directory that holds a 0.7.0 run. SCHEMA.md lists the layout. (c) The fail-first fixture asserts a non-empty Passes fact, the final status and no duplicate graphCheckOnly doc.'

problems.problem: The converge-marker step has the wrong target and an impossible measurement. (1) The spec packet does not get _BACKCHAIN_GATE_CONVERGE_ITEM. It gets _BACKCHAIN_ITEM_AUDIT with an empty marker, so its repair/revise child also loses the converge marker. (2) 'Measure hermetically what gate freeze sets from the packet' cannot be done, because freeze never reads the packet.
problems.evidence: Rendered with prompt() for both delegations: spec/converge and plan/converge both lack 'Backchain passes: converge', while spec/one, plan/one and spec/none carry 'Backchain passes: one'. _backchain_item (L2227-2238) passes `marker=_BACKCHAIN_ITEM_MARKER if _one_pass(...) else ""` for spec (the duty item at L1031). Only plan gets _BACKCHAIN_GATE_CONVERGE_ITEM (L2222-2224), and that text says 'required_trivial_reviews: 2' with no marker. _prompt_parts (L2427) skips _backchain_guidance for BACKCHAIN_FOLDED_STAGES, so _BACKCHAIN_PLAN_GATE_CONVERGE (L2084-2090) and _BACKCHAIN_AUDIT_CONVERGE reach no spec or plan packet. Yet test/shiploop-navigator-contract.test.py L3956 asserts the marker in `_backchain_guidance("plan","converge")`, which is dead text. freeze writes `required_trivial_reviews: GATES[passes]` (contract_for L498-537), and passes is `prepare --passes`, default 'default' (L1104), with GATES = {default:1, one:0, converge:2} (L66). Backchain SKILL.md L58-59 adds `--passes converge` only 'when the caller states that marker'. So the answer is already fixed by the code: by the documented rule a converge run's child gets the default gate, `required_trivial_reviews: 1` with EXIT_CONDITIONS['default']. Whether a host instead infers converge from 'required_trivial_reviews: 2' is a model choice that only a live run can show. Separately, the dry-run suite has no OnePassGateTests. Its Backchain tests are BackchainStageTextTests (shiploop-navigator-dry-run.test.py L511).
problems.fix: Rewrite the bullet: 'Today the converge plan item (_BACKCHAIN_GATE_CONVERGE_ITEM) and the converge spec item (_BACKCHAIN_ITEM_AUDIT, marker empty) carry no `Backchain passes: converge` line. By Backchain SKILL.md step 1 the host then runs `prepare` without `--passes`, and freeze writes `required_trivial_reviews: 1` (GATES["default"]). Converge has therefore meant Backchain's default gate since 0.7.0. Fail-first: assert that `prompt(stage, backchain_passes="converge")` for spec and plan, both delegations, contains `Backchain passes: converge`. Then give both items the converge marker, with the spec item mode-aware like _BACKCHAIN_AUDIT_CONVERGE.' Replace 'measure hermetically what gate freeze sets' with that reasoning. Change 'dry-run … OnePassGateTests' to 'dry-run BackchainStageTextTests'.

Then the quick tier, scripts/release.py --dry-run, the release'. release.py e2e_round_missing (L197-231) refuses a ShipLoop release unless every skills/shiploop/ commit precedes the range's latest test/shiploop_e2e/LEARNINGS.md commit. problems.problem: `export --run` as specified would export a run that finish called incomplete, and the digest it compares has no top-level field in result.json.
problems.evidence: verification() (backchain.py L833-850) checks the binding, the cycle records, that the plan is unchanged since the last record, and obligations. It never checks planning gaps or terminal status. finish sets `converged = status == "complete" and not problems and not gaps and receipt["ok"]` (L981) and writes `result["status"] = "converged" if converged else "incomplete"` (L1003). A stopped run, or a complete loop with planning gaps, can pass verify with a matching digest. result.json has no top-level output_sha256. It is result.convergence.candidate.output_sha256 (L988, L998) or, for caller runs, result.review.candidate.output_sha256 (L930, L1000).
problems.fix: Amend W3 item 4: 'Refuses (exit 1) unless DIR/result.json exists with `status == "converged"`, `verify` passes, and sha256(DIR/plan.json) equals `result.convergence.candidate.output_sha256` (or `result.review.candidate.output_sha256` for a caller run). A missing or unreadable result.json exits 3. Tests: export after an unrecorded edit, and export of a finished-incomplete run, are both refused.'

problems.problem: The edge-key guard does not close the collision it targets. The plan refuses only inherited IDs at prepare. A candidate can still add a step whose ID is 'null' (with allow_new_steps) and rewire a provisional `X<-null` key to it without allow_new_edges.
problems.evidence: I probed bound_errors in memory at origin/main. The inherited plan has X with input {need:'Fact X.', from:null}, with bounds provisional_step_ids [X], provisional_edge_keys ['X<-null'], allow_new_steps true and allow_new_edges false. The candidate adds step 'null' and sets X.inputs=[{need:'N done.', from:'null'}]. Result: bound_errors returns []. The same edit with ID 'N' returns ['new edge X<-N outside the edit bounds']. The cause is edge_key (L245-247), which writes None as 'null', together with bound_errors' key comparison (L292-305).
problems.fix: Amend W3 item 3: 'When edit_bounds is present, prepare refuses (exit 3) an inherited ID that contains `<-` or equals `null`. bound_errors (so freeze, record and verify) also reports any candidate step ID that does either. Tests: inherited `A<-B`, inherited `null`, and a new candidate step `null` used as a supplier.'

problems.problem: The noise precondition 'noise/√passes > δ' conflicts with how analyze already scales noise. Taken literally, it divides by √passes twice when noise is measured on the round, and not at all on the judges.json fallback.
problems.evidence: rubric_eval.py analyze: `noise = round(measured / passes ** 0.5, 2)` (L630) when pass noise is measured on the round. Otherwise `noise = judge_noise(...)` (L632) is a per-grading figure and is not divided. That value goes to decide(...) as `noise` (L692), and decide has no passes argument.
problems.fix: Amend W7 item 3: 'Use one per-mean noise figure: measured_pass_noise/√passes, or judges.json noise_points/√passes on the fallback (fix L632 to divide too). Block when that figure exceeds δ. decide receives it as is and never divides again. Report it as judge_noise_points.' Add a test where 3 passes give measured noise 6, so per-mean is 3.46, at δ 5: the case ships, where a second division (2.0) or the undivided fallback would decide differently.

problems.problem: 'critical: true criteria' assumes a rubric field that does not exist. Without a schema step, the critical-rise test cannot be written.
problems.evidence: grep 'critical' over skills/rubric-eval at origin/main finds nothing. Rubric criteria are `[name, text]` arrays (for example suites/architecture-v4/rubric.json 'criteria': {'P1': ['Proportion', '…']}). load_suite (L67) and SPEC §3 Suites (L50) define no critical flag. W7 lists only SPEC §1, §7, §8 and §10.
problems.fix: Add to W7: 'Rubric schema: an optional top-level `critical: [criterion IDs]` list. SPEC §3 states it, load_suite validates that each ID is a criterion, and existing suites keep working without it.' Make the test 'a critical-rise block' use a fixture suite that declares it.

problems.problem: The vendored ADAPTER.md edit, which makes the runtime-ephemeral.md read conditional on the parent-written route, also changes every ShipLoop loop stage. ShipLoop starts its loops through that same route. Neither release B's measurement nor its gate covers this.
problems.evidence: shiploop_loops.py binds the vendored improve/runtime/until-loop card (L38 and runtime() at L472). It prints 'Contract: … · Receipt: …' and start_command (L583-605), which is the 'Start from a parent-written contract' route (ADAPTER.md L39-62). The read the plan targets is at ADAPTER.md L189, in '## Follow the returned action' (L135), which that route follows. release.py e2e_round_missing asks for a round only for skills/shiploop/ and changes/shiploop/ (L215-216), so a skills/improve/ edit triggers no round. W4's measurement is only Backchain cohort B's trace counts.
problems.fix: Add to W4: 'This card is also ShipLoop's loop card (shiploop_loops.runtime). The ADAPTER.md/PROVENANCE commit lands before release B's ShipLoop E2E round (the D-D round). That round's LEARNINGS entry records whether ShipLoop loop stages read runtime-ephemeral.md and whether any stage then failed a recovery or report-shape step that file covers. lenses.overall:
The W2, W3 items 1-2 and 5, W4 (prepare cross-references, the SKILL.md scope, the lenses-style section fetch), W5 and W8 symbols exist at origin/main and mostly behave as the plan assumes. Line numbers are within a few lines of the plan's: SKILL.md 174-176, protocol.md 269/282, orchestrator-test-map.md:24, prepare at L553-624, decide at L512, analyze at L593, find_backchain_loops at L1153, resolved_backchain_resources at L1977, ADAPTER.md 68/189.

Ten problems are material.
- W9 is already done (39b417c26d24f2344a7b6c84617f8b94a9a554b8), so its fail-first test cannot fail.
- W1's run-review export fix needs loop_doc, the graph-check classifier and a defined Backchain run directory, not just the finder.
- W1's converge fix misses the spec packet. Its 'hermetic measurement' is answered by the code itself: freeze takes the gate from `prepare --passes`, never from the packet. Without the marker the documented gate is the default `required_trivial_reviews: 1`, so converge has silently meant 1 since 0.7.0.
- W6's tools (audit.py, metrics.py stage-share) cannot read ShipLoop E2E runs or give tokens per review, and run.py cannot set converge mode.
- W6's heading contradicts the release order.
- W3's `export --run` must require `status == converged`, and W3's edge-key guard must also cover candidate-added IDs (probe-confirmed hole).
- W7's noise precondition double-scales by √passes, and its `critical` criteria have no rubric field.
- W4's ADAPTER edit silently changes ShipLoop's own loop stages.

Fix those plan texts before W0.

problems.problem: W6 cannot produce the measurement D-D needs, and it may not exercise W1 at all. Five gaps. (1) run.py has no option that puts a run in converge mode. (2) Nothing makes the host request the plan-stage Backchain child. (3) The template's request is a toy one. (4) The named readers cannot read an E2E run folder. (5) --source checkout builds uncommitted edits.
problems.evidence: (1) Converge is the ShipLoop start flag `--backchain-passes` (shiploop_protocol.py:236). run.py's arguments (run.py:2510-2640) have no such option. Its only precedent is planning_review_sentence (run.py:405-408), which appends a start-option sentence for --planning-review. (2) _BACKCHAIN_PLAN_CHOICE (shiploop_prompts.py:2115-2122) and _BACKCHAIN_PLAN_CHOICE_ITEM (2211) say: "nothing refuses a plan without it, and ShipLoop cannot see whether the child ran". The converge text has no requirement either. (3) The template docs/experiments/follow-on-recommended-gap-20261101/launch.sh runs a slug.py deferral request with `--source marketplace`. That is a one- or two-step plan, which gives a second review little to find. (4) docs/experiments/backchain-efficiency-20261101/audit.py reads `--study` (default /Users/dadleet/src/backchain/results/full-workflow-20261016, L27). It needs decision-analysis.json (L134-136) and runs/*/summary.json plus artifacts/loop/report*.json (run_record L54-96), and an E2E output has neither. metrics.py stage_share (L3272-3307) returns seconds only, with no tokens and no per-review split. For Codex, tokens exist only as rollout windows (planning_tokens L1422-1427). (5) build_candidate (run.py:560-564) is 'working-tree changes included', but the run records only local_head (L494).
problems.fix: Rewrite W6. The arranged request states two sentences: 'Start ShipLoop with --backchain-passes converge' (or one), and 'At plan, request one Backchain plan/draft child'. Use a request with real dependency structure (a brownfield case such as tickets-assign), not the slug template. Pre-register an inclusion rule: a run counts only if run state records backchain_passes equal to its arm, and run/backchain/<action>/ holds a 0.7.0 loop/receipt.json with the expected gate. Otherwise rerun it, and report excluded runs. Read the per-cycle review classes with W1's fixed Run Review exporter (find_backchain_loops, export.py:1153) or a new committed reader with a test, not audit.py. Take seconds per review from the child's record/done call timestamps. Take tokens from Codex rollout windows between those bounds, or write 'tokens per review: unmeasured'. Launch only from a clean worktree at the committed W1+W3 head, and record plugin_sha256 in each LEARNINGS entry.

problems.problem: W9 has already landed on origin/main. As written it cannot meet the plan's rule that every new test first fails at the base. It also answers the merge question the wrong way: --no-merges hides the merge commit itself, but release.py still lists every non-merge ShipLoop commit that a merge brings in when that commit is not reachable from the latest LEARNINGS commit.

It is the only commit after f5fb7d64 that touches any W-path. The range used is `journal..HEAD` (release.py:213-216), which is a reachability test.
problems.fix: Delete W9 and cite 39b417c2 as the gate in force. Add this to the release A order: the last commit touching test/shiploop_e2e/LEARNINGS.md must come after the final merge of origin/main into the branch. If main gains ShipLoop commits after the W6 entry, add another LEARNINGS entry after the re-merge that says which round covers them.

problems.problem: The release A sequence leaves out steps and places the E2E round where later commits can strip its coverage. Four problems. (1) The Review Coverage loop runs 'after implement' with up to 12 rounds and a wrap-up commit, and nothing places it before W6, so a ShipLoop fix made by that loop lands after the LEARNINGS commit. (2) W6's heading says '(after release A)', while 'Order and dependencies' and W6's own text make W6 part of release A. (3) There is no step to merge the branch into main. (4) There is no publish step.
problems.evidence: See e2e_round_missing (release.py:197-232). The Review Coverage section reads: 'After implement ... Loop one round after another ... apply remaining Deferred ... trivial improvements in one pathspec wrap-up commit'. The release.py module docstring says: 'It never pushes. Publish the commit with scripts/release-push.py.' AGENTS.md: 'Merge verified work directly to main'. A routine release needs 'preflight and CI pass on a commit that fast-forwards main'.
problems.fix: Replace the release A order with this sequence. (1) W1, W2 and W3 commits. (2) review-converge rounds on the release A paths, including the wrap-up commit. (3) Merge origin/main into the branch. (4) W6 runs from the clean worktree at that head. (5) The LEARNINGS commit, as the last commit touching skills/shiploop/ or changes/shiploop/. (6) The quick tier. (7) Merge the branch into main; if main moved with ShipLoop commits, add a new LEARNINGS entry. (8) release.py --dry-run, then release.py. (9) scripts/release-push.py. (10) CI on main. (11) Host refresh. (12) Remove the worktree. Change W6's heading to '(part of release A; D-D after it)'.

problems.problem: W3 ships model-read prompt changes in release A without a cohort. The clearest case is W3.5, where `record` prints a done line meant to change behaviour (the 10 of 31 hand-written submitters). The convergence.md and caller-contract.md text edits are also model-read. Cohort B's control is release A, so W3.5's effect is built into both arms and is never measured. The audit's INSTRUCTIONS list (audit.py:31-37) counts convergence.md and caller-contract.md as instruction files. Verifier R7-R8: 'A new record stdout line is model-visible text ... none should be claimed without the cohort's paired grading.' W1 is ShipLoop text, which falls outside D2's Backchain cohort, so its E2E round is the right route.
problems.fix: Move W3.5 into cohort B's candidate arm (release B). Limit release A's convergence.md and caller-contract.md edits to stating what the new script refusals enforce. Alternatively, add owner decision D-E: 'Does D2 cover script stdout and doc text that only states a new mechanical refusal?' Record the answer in Round 10 before release A.

problems.problem: Cohort B names no runner, subject or grader, and its candidate code has no branch. The runner and model choice needs an owner decision. Unaccepted candidate code has no stated home off main. D-C's case count would amend D2 without saying so.
problems.evidence: D2 (journal L20-22) fixes 'gpt-6-astra medium through Codex' with about 10 cases. D3 (journal L242-244) exempted only 'this cohort' from the standing rule that every live-model measurement goes through run.py on Terra xhigh (memory use-the-codex-harness: 'Exception ... the Backchain efficiency cohort'). W4 and W5 are written alongside the case set, so the candidate's author can see new held-out cases before the freeze. Its 'Order of work' (L112-123) is: pilot, adversarial review, freeze, run, grade, analyze, and 'No candidate change after the freeze'. problems.evidence: resolved_backchain_resources lists improve/runtime/until-loop/ADAPTER.md and runtime-ephemeral.md as required child resources (shiploop_prompts.py:1988-1991). lenses.overall:
The plan's direction is sound, but it is not ready to execute as written. Four problems carry the most weight:

lenses.overall: The plan puts the right questions to the owner. D-A (it changes rubric-eval's default and breaks comparability), D-C (the owner's acceptable loss and the cohort size) and D-D (the number of ShipLoop Backchain reviews, an 'ask first' item) are all owner decisions. The two-release split is correctly called routine: AGENTS.md Decisions makes releases routine once the preflight and CI pass, and A comes before cohort B rather than in the middle of it, so batch-run-to-completion holds. D-B's first branch (fix the oracle and keep the 2026-10-17 rule) is itself routine because it preserves an earlier decision. Only the pilot exception needs the owner. Two concerns raised in the brief do not hold. First, no re-vendor is pending: upstream until-loop main is 332bd11, which is exactly what PROVENANCE.json vendors (0.10.1), so the memory index line is stale. Second, an optional edit_bounds key whose absence means today's behaviour is a permission, not a legacy mode, so 'one supported version' allows it. W6 follows 'measure through run.py on Codex Terra'. W1's converge-marker fix restores D1 rather than changing it. The real problems are silent departures from standing rules. (1) The vendored ADAPTER.md edit changes every ShipLoop and Improve loop, and no gate or measurement covers that. (2) Release A ships model-visible Backchain text without a cohort; W3.5 is the clearest case. (3) Unaccepted candidate code has no stated home off main, and W7 is held back from release, which blocks other sessions' marketplace launches. (4) Cohort B extends D3 without asking and drops D2's adversarial review and pilot. (5) The W6 ordering contradicts itself, and the review-converge rounds are unplaced, so the preflight can refuse release A. (6) W9 already shipped in 39b417c2. (7) CI will reject W4 and W5 for missing change notes. (8) D-A does not tell the owner it reverses their 2026-09-27 rule. (9) The plan does not coordinate with the F31 session, which is live and edits the same files. (10) The runner moves into the public repo, a KISS-violating edge-key guard is added, and route tests are missing. With these fixes to the plan text, it is consistent with the recorded rules.
